response.evidence: A rough manual count (not exact) shows White male applicants were denied about 6% of the time (about 15 denials out of roughly 230-250 applications). That is at or below the overall denial rate of about 8-9%. It is also well below the rates for Hispanic male, Black, and several other groups, where denials appear more frequent. Most White male denials coincide with high debt-to-income ratios (50%+ or over 60%), zero reported income, or loan-to-value ratios near 100%, which are non-demographic risk factors. It shows no controlled comparison, so it cannot rule out discrimination entirely, but it gives no evidence of it.
